Privileged access recertification is performed every quarter. System owners review the privileged account inventory, and managers certify that each account still has a valid business purpose. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all privileged sessions.

New access requires a ticket, manager approval, and system-owner approval before activation. Access belonging to a terminated worker must be disabled within 24 hours of the separation notice. Security Operations reviews overdue removals each week.

A Severity 1 incident must be reported to the incident commander within 15 minutes of confirmation. The commander opens the incident channel, assigns an owner, and records major decisions in the incident timeline.

A post-incident review must be completed within five business days after service restoration. The review records root cause, corrective actions, and owners. Investigation evidence and the final review are retained for two years.

Every vendor receives a documented risk assessment before onboarding. The assessment covers data access, service criticality, security controls, and subcontractors. Critical vendors require approval from Procurement and Security.

Critical vendors are reassessed annually. Contracts must require notification of a confirmed data breach within 48 hours. Evidence of assessments, approvals, and remediation is retained for the life of the contract plus three years.

Finance records are retained for seven years. Human Resources records are retained for six years after employment ends. Customer support recordings are retained for 18 months unless a longer period is required by contract.

A legal hold suspends normal deletion for affected records until Legal releases the hold. Automated deletion jobs run every quarter, and record owners review purge exceptions within ten business days.

An itemized receipt is required for any expense above 75 dollars. Employees submit expenses within ten calendar days, and the direct manager approves the business purpose before Finance processes reimbursement.

Air travel must use economy class unless an executive approves an exception. Personal purchases, commuting costs, and minibar charges are not reimbursable.

Full-time employees receive 20 days of annual leave each year. Planned leave of five days or more should be requested at least two weeks in advance. Managers consider team coverage before approval.

A medical certificate is required after more than two consecutive sick days. Up to five unused annual-leave days may be carried into the next year; additional unused days expire.

Remote workers must connect through the corporate VPN before accessing internal systems. Public Wi-Fi may be used only when the VPN is active. Company devices automatically lock after ten minutes of inactivity. Confidential calls must not be conducted where unauthorized people can hear them. Lost devices must be reported to the service desk within one hour.

A normal production change requires a change ticket, documented test evidence, peer review, and approval from the service owner before deployment. The implementer records the outcome and any rollback action in the ticket. Emergency changes require incident-commander approval and a retrospective review within two business days.

The customer portal has a recovery time objective of two hours. Payroll has a recovery time objective of four hours. Business owners validate recovery priorities during continuity exercises, which are conducted twice each year.

Production backups run daily and are encrypted before leaving the primary environment. Restore tests are performed every quarter. Crisis contact lists are reviewed monthly, and failed restore tests require a corrective-action owner within three business days.

New starters must complete security awareness training within 30 days of joining and repeat it annually. The Security team conducts phishing simulations every quarter and reports aggregate results to leadership.
Suspected phishing messages must be reported to Security within one hour and must not be opened or forwarded. Anyone who fails a simulation completes remedial training within ten business days.
